title: Sebastian and the Choir Anew
premise: When the valley's protective wards collapse on the night the stars vanish, beast-speaker Astrid Iversen is dragged beyond the only world she has ever known, pursued by the Choir — a cabal of mages who once silenced all wild magic and now hunt the last speakers to fuel their fading power. Guided by a wounded griffin and a defector from the Choir, Astrid discovers her gift can either restore the fallen stars or crown a new tyrant, and that survival may demand she become the very thing she fears. In the end, Astrid chooses to pour her gift into the sky itself, extinguishing her own magic but reigniting the stars and shattering the Choir's dominion — earning not power, but a place among those who finally see her.
about_author: Lena Marchetti is the pen name of a former choir singer turned fantasy novelist who grew up in a Norwegian fishing village where the mountains were said to keep secrets. She writes about outsiders, old magic, and the cost of belonging.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgot Magic
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. We meet her in the hidden valley, secretly speaking with a lame fox while hiding her gift from a community that exiled speakers generations ago. The emotional beat is quiet longing — she belongs nowhere, even at home.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The wards fail with a sound like breaking glass; the stars vanish one by one; a wounded griffin crashes into her family's barn pursued by hooded riders. Terror and awe arrive together as her sheltered life ends.

chapters.title: What the Griffin Brought
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The dying griffin, Ashveil, names her 'speaker' and begs rescue in words only she can hear. Her mother burns her childhood drawings of talking animals, revealing she always knew. The beat: betrayal braided with fierce maternal love.

chapters.title: Riders in the Pass
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The Choir's hunters reach the valley; Astrid flees with Ashveil through collapsing mountain passes, leaving her family behind. First taste of guilt — escape purchased with someone else's sacrifice.

chapters.title: A World Without Stars
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Beyond the valley, she sees the wider land: crops failing, beasts gone silent and mad under a starless sky. The world is dying slowly, and everyone blames the last wild speakers. Beat: dawning scale of the crisis.

chapters.title: The Defector
chapters.summary: Alternating POV introducing Corin Hale, a Choir cantor who faked his death and now shadows Astrid. He saves her from an ambush but cannot explain why. His chapter carries shame and a secret debt he intends to repay with her trust.

chapters.title: An Uneasy Alliance
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Forced to travel with Corin after he proves the ambushers weren't his doing, she tests him through the animals, who smell his lies and his grief in equal measure. Beat: wary, prickly trust beginning to form.

chapters.title: The Choir's Song
chapters.summary: Corin's POV. Flashback reveals the Choir's origin: mages who bound their voices into a single Song to end an ancient war, then discovered the Song feeds on speaker-gifts — and the stars were its first victims. Beat: horror at complicity.

chapters.title: City of Bells
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The trio reaches Vesperhold, the Choir's capital, where bells replace birdsong and citizens hum the Song in their sleep. Astrid poses as a mute servant. Beat: suffocating conformity, and her first glimpse of the Choir's Maestro.

chapters.title: The Archive Beneath
chapters.summary: Corin's POV. He leads them into forbidden archives proving the stars are imprisoned voices — every speaker the Choir ever consumed. Astrid realizes her gift could free them or bind them tighter. Beat: the weight of choice lands.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Bell Tower
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A trap springs: Corin's defection was known, and his capture was the bait. Astrid escapes with Ashveil but abandons Corin to the Maestro's hands. Beat: rage, heartbreak, and the bitter logic of survival.

chapters.title: Wild Country
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Grieving, she shelters among feral beasts gone half-mad without starlight, learning to calm them — discovering her gift grows stronger as the sky darkens. Beat: transformation; she stops apologizing for what she is.

chapters.title: The Maestro's Offer
chapters.summary: Maestro Solenne's POV. Through Corin's imprisonment we learn her plan: consume Astrid's gift to complete the Song, ending magic forever — including the hunger that will otherwise devour the Choir. Beat: chillingly sympathetic villainy.

chapters.title: What Corin Chose
chapters.summary: Corin's POV. Tortured for Astrid's location, Corin sings false notes into the Choir's network, poisoning the Song from within at terrible personal cost. Beat: redemption purchased with pain; hope rekindled.

chapters.title: The Gathering Silence
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The beasts lead her to the First Hollow, where the stars' stolen voices pool underground like buried light. Ashveil reveals the price: opening it requires a speaker to give up their gift entirely. Beat: dread and resolve entwined.

chapters.title: Hunters at the Hollow
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge. The Choir descends on the Hollow; Astrid's beast-allies hold the line in a desperate, bloody defense. Corin escapes captivity mid-battle to reach her side. Beat: chaos, loyalty proven under fire.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Cornered, Astrid faces the choice: flee and live voiceless-but-free, or open the Hollow and lose everything. She remembers her mother burning the drawings and chooses to stop running. Beat: the theme made flesh.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the First Hollow
chapters.summary: Climax, Astrid and Solenne POVs alternating. Above the pooled starlight, Astrid and the Maestro duel with song and silence; Corin unravels the Choir's binding from below. Solenne offers Astrid shared power — and Astrid refuses. Beat: the corrupting offer declined.

chapters.title: Letting Go of the Gift
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She pours her speaker-gift into the Hollow; the stolen voices rise as returning stars, and the Choir's Song collapses into ordinary music. Ashveil dies becoming the first new constellation. Beat: sacrifice, grief, transcendence.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Corin's POV. The Choir dissolves; some cantors kneel, some flee. Corin, half-deafened by the Song's death, chooses exile over power and asks nothing of Astrid. Beat: quiet reckoning with what he owes and can never repay.

chapters.title: Homecoming, Changed
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Magicless now, she returns to the valley to find the wards rebuilt by neighbors who finally know her secret — and accept her anyway. Her mother's apology is wordless and complete. Beat: belonging earned, not granted.

chapters.title: Sebastian and the Choir Anew
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Astrid's POV. Years later, children speak of a fox named Sebastian who still seems to understand them, though no magic remains. Astrid smiles, keeping one last small secret: some gifts outlive their givers. Beat: warm, wry closure.
